title: Credential Ops guide for SDKs: rotation flows, streaming reauth, and safe retry patterns
creator: Avery Chen
description: Goal: Deliver a cross-language (Python/TypeScript/Go) Credential Operations (CredOps) guide and SDK primitives that make API key rotation, SSO token handoff, streaming reauthentication, and secret handling safe and ergonomic for developers and platform teams. The scope includes: (1) SDK-level token provider interfaces for ephemeral credentials and SSO token refresh, (2) safe retry/backoff strategies that do not duplicate side-effects during credential handoffs, (3) streaming client patterns that transparently resume after reauth (where feasible), (4) recommended local dev and CI secret provider patterns (env, secret store adapters, devbox integration), and (5) sample migration recipes and docs for enterprise customers. Deliverables: design doc, language-specific SDK changes and examples, test harness for rotation scenarios, and migration playbook for Dedicated/Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Public SDKs expose a standardized TokenProvider abstraction with language idiomatic implementations and unit tests. 2) Rotation test harness simulates mid-stream token expiry and demonstrates graceful resume or clear error with deterministic retry hints. 3) Docs include clear migration steps for rotating API keys without downtime for hosted and dedicated customers. 4) CI/local dev guidance and quickstart snippets available for each language. 5) Security review sign-off and a minimal cookbook of observability metrics (auth-failures, rotation-latency, streaming-resumes).
design_decisions: Use a TokenProvider interface inserted at the transport layer (HTTP client middleware / interceptor) to centralize refresh and caching
Prefer background refresh with proactive refresh window (e.g., refresh when 10% of TTL remains) to avoid thundering refreshes
For streaming responses, attempt transparent reauth+resume only if the model/runtime supports resuming with token swap; otherwise fail with deterministic retryable error and guidance
Expose opt-in developer hooks to persist ephemeral credentials to devbox secret stores or CI secret managers; never default to long-lived filesystem secrets
Backoff policy: use jittered exponential backoff with capped retries and idempotency keys for requests that mutate state
Minimal breaking change strategy: add TokenProvider as optional parameter with sensible default using env var API_KEY to remain backwards compatible
implementation_notes:
- Python: add TokenProvider protocol and aiohttp/requests auth adapter; streaming client to surface on_reauth callback.
- TypeScript: middleware for fetch/node-fetch and streaming TransformStream-friendly reauth strategy.
- Go: context-based token provider injected into http.Client RoundTripper with concurrency-safe cache and singleflight refresh.
- Add integration tests that spin up a test server that invalidates tokens mid-stream and a harness that verifies backpressure and resume behaviour.
- Provide examples: rotating API key with zero-downtime using canary key rollout + verification call, SSO token exchange example for enterprise SAML -> short-lived token, CI secret rotation recipe.
- Observability: emit metrics auth.token_refresh.count, auth.token_refresh.latency_ms, auth.stream.resume.count, auth.failures.rate and traces for refresh paths.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Transparent resume not supported by all protocols -> Mitigation: detect resume capability and fall back to fail-fast with retry guidance
Risk: Background refresh causing thundering herd on servers -> Mitigation: use jitter and singleflight dedupe on refresh across threads/processes
Risk: Developers persist long-lived secrets unintentionally -> Mitigation: docs + linters/examples that discourage writing keys to repo or plain files and provide devbox secret adapter
Risk: Migration complexity for Dedicated/Private customers -> Mitigation: provide scripted migration playbooks and an opt-in compatibility shim for old credentials
tasks: Write cross-language TokenProvider spec and example implementations
Implement Python auth adapter and add streaming reauth hook
Implement TypeScript middleware and streaming resume pattern example
Implement Go RoundTripper with singleflight refresh and concurrency tests
Create rotation test harness and integration tests
Draft migration playbook for Dedicated/Private customers
Add docs and quickstart snippets to developer portal
Run security review and address findings
